correctness.rationale: Using the published properly colored rooted-tree characterization, splitting rank equals the count of black vertices because the operator satisfies R²=-λR and is triangular with diagonal 0 or -λ. For a fixed black set allowed trees are spanning trees of K_(1,k,n-k); matrix-tree eigenvalues yield the exact formula. Root expansion to a specified edge gives the known univariate total. Stirling expansion with Φ(x)=(1-2x)log(x/(1-x)) and Φ(1/2+u)=-8u²+O(u⁴) gives the normalized local Gaussian law with variance 1/16. Independent matrix-equation and Prüfer enumerations pass for small n. The infinite claims rest on proof, not numerics.

value.rationale: For splitting Rota–Baxter operators, rank records the dimension of one algebra summand in a complete decomposition of F^n; the source reports totals and orbits but not this refinement. The exact field-independent full rank spectrum and local normal limit quantify how strongly the two summands balance, with variance n/16 rather than the usual binomial n/4. An exact all-rank classification and asymptotic fluctuations are natural invariants of the motivating operators rather than an arbitrary small finite calculation.
